item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study of pediatric AAs between 2000 and 2020, approval frequently relied on surrogate end points and extrapolation with pharmacokinetic bridging studies, with limited pediatric enrollment. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the significant association of individual, familial, and societal factors with Korean adolescent drug use. item.title: Oncologic efficacy and safety of stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer: a systemic meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis indicates that SBRT yields favorable treatment outcomes for patients with oligometastatic NSCLC with manageable toxicities. When anatomically feasible, delivering an ablative dose-100 Gy(10) in biologically effective dose-is recommended. Furthermore, tailoring SBRT strategies by oligometastatic subtype-upfront radical SBRT for synchronous disease/ORD and salvage SBRT for OPSD/OPD-is essential to maximize the treatment efficacy.

item.description: OBJECTIVE: Occupational noise exposure and psychological distress are significant occupational health risks faced by working women, both of which may affect reproductive health. This study aimed to investigate the correlational pathways and interaction patterns linking occupational noise exposure levels, psychological distress, and reproductive aging among perimenopausal female workers.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The adapted procedure measures task-specific listening level requirements in CIs. Findings indicate that listening levels vary with the listening task and acoustic environment, supporting assessment of listening levels during SI rather than passive listening.

item.title: Associations Between Traffic Noise Exposure and Cardiometabolic Disease for Park Visitors Aged 45-64
item.description: CONCLUSION: Residential noise exposure above 55.7 dB increases CMD risk in residents aged 45-64 years. The impact of traffic noise exposure on CMD risk might be partially mitigated through regular walking in city parks.

item.title: Associations of Cumulative Noise Exposure with Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, and Stress Hormones in Female Workers
item.description: CONCLUSION: Occupational noise exposure was independently associated with elevated blood pressure and reduced HR among female workers. However, no statistically significant mediating effects of the six stress hormones were identified in the associations between occupational noise exposure and blood pressure or HR.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Considerable inter-institutional and regional variation was observed in cytogenetic detection rates. CA detected abnormalities more frequently than MN assays. item.title: Managing Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth in Pediatric Short Bowel Syndrome: A Consensus Statement
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This Delphi-based consensus provides the first international pediatric-specific guidance for diagnosing and managing SIBO in children with SBS. Implementation of these recommendations may reduce practice variability, support more judicious antibiotic use, and improve patient outcomes while establishing a foundation for future research in this high-risk population.
